problems.title: Count a closed integer interval
problems.question: How many integers satisfy |x|≤3?
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: $|x|\le3$ means $-3\le x\le3$.
steps: The integers are −3,−2,−1,0,1,2,3.

problems.title: Sum two absolute-value roots
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of |2x−1|=7.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
steps: The roots are 4 and −3; their sum is 1.

problems.title: Range of a square plus one
problems.question: Find the range of a²+1 for −3<a<5.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: The square has minimum 0 at a=0 and approaches 25 as a→5⁻.
steps: Thus 0≤a²<25. All these square values are attained using nonnegative a<5. Add 1.

problems.title: Contact chord in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base 12. The distance between incircle contact points on the equal sides is 4. Find each equal side.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: If each equal side is l, the tangent segment from the apex is l−6. The contact chord is parallel to the base, with similarity ratio $(l-6)/l=4/12$.
steps: 3(l−6)=l gives 2l=18.

problems.title: Nearest circle point
problems.question: A point is 15 from a circle centre and 8 from the nearest circle point. Which listed radius is possible?
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: The nearest distance is $|15-r|=8$.
steps: Thus r=7 or 23. Only 23 appears among the printed choices.
problems.answer: Listed answer:23; both possible radii are 7 and 23.

problems.title: An absolute expression at most zero
problems.question: How many roots has $|5(x^2-9)(x+4)(x+1)/[(x+3)(x-2)]|\le0$?
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: An absolute value is ≤0 only if the expression is 0. The domain excludes x=−3,2.
steps: The numerator zeros are −3,3,−4,−1. Remove the excluded−3, leaving 3,−4,−1.

problems.title: Equal absolute values
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of |3x−1|=|x+5|.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: The two possibilities are $3x-1=x+5$ or $3x-1=-(x+5)$.
steps: They give x=3 and x=−1. Both satisfy the original equation.

problems.title: Cancel a large common power
problems.question: Evaluate $(5^{n+2}-5^n)/(5^{n+2}+5^{n+1}+2\cdot5^n)$ for $n=5^3-1$.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: Factor the nonzero common $5^n$ from numerator and denominator.
steps: The quotient becomes(25−1)/(25+5+2)=24/32. The value of n has no effect.

problems.title: A multiplicative percentage change
problems.question: Compare $(a^2-9)a^3b^7c^4/(a+3)$ with $(5a-15)a^7b^9c^4/(a^4b^2)$ on their common domain.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: The first simplifies to $(a-3)a^3b^7c^4$ and the second to $5(a-3)a^3b^7c^4$.
steps: The target is 5 times the initial expression. Where the initial value is nonzero, the relative change is(5−1)·100%=400%.
problems.answer: Multiply by 5; the usual listed answer is a 400% increase.
problems.note: If the initial value is 0, both expressions are 0 and a relative percentage is undefined. For negative values, “increase” is ambiguous in ordinary language; the exact algebraic statement is multiplication by 5.

problems.title: Distance between two altitude feet
problems.question: In acute ABC, AA₁ and BB₁ are altitudes. CA₁=6, AC=10, AB=9. Find A₁B₁.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: The altitude-foot triangles give $A_1B_1/AB=\cos C=CA_1/AC$.
steps: Thus cos C=6/10=3/5 and A₁B₁=9·3/5.

problems.title: A 36-degree isosceles triangle
problems.question: AB=BC and B=36°. Bisector AD has length a and CD=b. Find perimeter ABC.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: Angles A, C are 72°, while BAD=DAC=36°. Triangle ACD has angles 36°,72°,72°, hence AC=AD=a.
steps: Triangle ABD has angles 36°,36°,108°, so BD=AD=a. Thus BC=BD+DC=a+b and AB=a+b. Add all three sides.

problems.title: Eight natural solutions
problems.question: Which listed a makes x>a, x<9 have eight natural-number solutions?
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: With natural numbers $1,2,3,\ldots$, the eight possible values below 9 are 1,…,8. All occur exactly when $a<1$.
steps: The printed values −1.3,−0.3 and 0.3 are all less than 1 and all work. The other listed values exclude at least 1.
problems.answer: All a<1; three listed answers are −1.3,−0.3,0.3.
problems.note: If a convention includes 0 among natural numbers, exactly eight solutions requires 0≤a<1, making 0.3 the sole listed choice. The positive-natural convention gives multiple valid choices.

problems.title: Similar triangles from an angle condition
problems.question: D lies on AC and ABD=BCA. AB=8, AC=10. Find AD.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: Triangles ABD and ACB share angle A and have the stated second equal angle. Thus $AD/AB=AB/AC$.
steps: AD=AB²/AC=64/10.

problems.title: A parallel cuts a triangle
problems.question: MN∥AC cuts AB, BC at M, N. BN: NC=3:7 and AC=20. Find MN.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: The similarity ratio is $BN/BC=3/(3+7)=3/10$.
steps: Multiply AC by 3/10.

problems.title: Minimum of a product minus a variable
problems.question: Find min(ab−c) for −3≤a≤6,−4≤b≤5,−1≤c≤9.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: The extreme values of ab on this rectangle occur at corners:12,−15,−24,30.
steps: The least product is −24 at a=6, b=−4. To minimise ab−c, choose the largest c=9. These choices are simultaneous.

problems.title: Perimeter of a coordinate rectangle
problems.question: The region |x+1|≤6,|y|≤a has perimeter 32. Find a.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: The x-interval is $[-7,5]$, width 12. For a>0 the height is 2a, so $P=2(12+2a)$.
steps: Set 24+4a=32, giving a=2. It gives a nondegenerate rectangle as required.

problems.title: Ordering powers across one
problems.question: Order $a=x,b=x^{15}/x^{12},c=x^{11}/x^5,d=x^{17}/x^3$ increasingly for 0<x<7.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: The values are $x,x^3,x^6,x^{14}$.
steps: For 0<x<1, larger powers are smaller, giving d<c<b<a. For 1<x<7, the order reverses to a<b<c<d. At x=1 all are equal.
problems.answer: No single order is determined on(0,7).

problems.title: Similar triangles across parallel lines
problems.question: AB∥CD and segments AD, BC meet at O. AB=5, CD=20, OB=3. Find BC.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: Triangles AOB and DOC are similar, so $OB/OC=AB/CD=1/4$.
steps: OC=12. Because O is on both crossing segments, BC=BO+OC.

problems.title: Sum of two parallel sections
problems.question: Two parallels to AC divide AB from vertex B in ratios 2:9 and 5:6. AC=44. Find the sum of their segments inside ABC.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: The similarity fractions from B are $2/11$ and $5/11$.
steps: The section lengths are 44·2/11=8 and 44·5/11=20. Add them.

problems.title: Integer intersection of two inequalities
problems.question: How many integers satisfy |x+1|<|2x−5| and |x|≤7?
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
steps: Thus x<4/3 or x>6. Inside[−7,7], the integers are −7,…,1 and 7:9+1 values.

problems.title: A common ratio involving a repeating decimal
problems.question: If $a/m=b/n=c/k=1/(1+0.\overline3)$, which listed interval contains $5(m+n+k)/(a+b+c)$?
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: $0.\overline3=1/3$, so each ratio is 3/4. Consequently $a+b+c=(3/4)(m+n+k)$.
steps: Where the requested quotient is defined, it equals 5·4/3=20/3, which lies strictly between 6 and 7.

problems.title: Maximum vertical separation in a region
problems.question: A, B both satisfy y≥−2x+3, y≥x−9, y≤−x+11. Find max(y₁−y₂).
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: The bounded region is a triangle. Its vertices are intersections of the three boundary lines.
steps: The vertices are(−8,19),(4,−5),(10,1). The maximum y is 19 and minimum −5, attained independently by the two points. Their difference is 24.

problems.title: An inequality true for an entire half-line
problems.question: Find all a such that 5−4x≥a+2 for every x≤4.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: The left side decreases with x, so its minimum on $(-\infty,4]$ occurs at x=4.
steps: Require 5−16≥a+2, or −11≥a+2. This is also sufficient for every smaller x.

problems.title: Ratios of crossing chords
problems.question: Chords AB, CD intersect at K, with AK/KB=2/9 and DK/KB=1/8. DB=7. Find AC.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
formulas: Triangles AKC and DKB are similar: the K angles are vertical and the other angles intercept equal circle arcs. Thus $AC/DB=AK/DK$.
steps: The ratio AK/DK=(2/9)/(1/8)=16/9. Multiply DB=7 by 16/9.
problems.note: The printed choices omit 112/9. The given ratios determine this value; no listed numerical choice matches it.

problems.title: A point dividing a segment
problems.question: BM=4AM, with A=(7,2), B=(−3,12). Find the coordinate sum of M.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra or similarity, keeping all domain restrictions.
